description:
Scaffold the multi-version stack at `base_dir`: a docker-compose.yml (one shared Postgres 16 +
    one odoo:<major> per version in `versions`), one odoo<major>.conf each (with the shared-Postgres
    isolation baked in: db_name + dbfilter + list_db=False), non-colliding host ports (http 80xx /
    gevent 81xx), named volumes, and a chmod-600 .secrets (generated DB + admin/master password).
    `enterprise` = the majors to run as EE. For an official image their conf gets the
    /mnt/enterprise addons path (run docker_ee_mount for each before docker_db_init).
    `local_images` = the majors that run from a LOCALLY BUILT image (docker_image_build) instead
    of the official one - required for a major with no official image yet (20). A local major
    runs `odoo-local:<m>-ee` when it is also in `enterprise`, else `odoo-local:<m>-ce` (build that
    edition first; an older edition-less `odoo-local:<m>` of the right edition is adopted).
    DATABASE IMAGE: with any Enterprise major the shared db runs pgvector/pgvector (Postgres 16 +
    the `vector` extension that Odoo 19/20 Enterprise AI and 20's own MCP server `ai_mcp` need);
    a Community-only stack keeps postgres:16. Switching an existing stack is safe: same Postgres
    major, the data volume is checked (PG_VERSION) before anything is written, and once a stack
    runs pgvector it keeps it. Neutral, no branding on the box. Idempotent-ish:
    re-running overwrites the compose+confs (safe) but keeps the .secrets/volumes. dry_run shows all
    the files it would write. `port_base` (default 8000: http 80<major>, gevent 81<major>) moves the
    host ports when the box already uses them - check `ss -ltn` first on a box with other services
    (then pass the same port_base to docker_domain).

    ADDING A MAJOR to an existing stack (e.g. a source-version reference container next to a
    test stack of the new version): just re-run with the longer `versions`. An existing
    <service>.conf is KEPT when it differs from the generated one (your hand edits survive -
    reported in `kept_confs`); `overwrite_confs=true` replaces it after a timestamped backup.
    The compose file is regenerated (it is ours); the limits override and .secrets are kept.

    `limits` (optional): {service|major|'db': {"cpus": 2, "mem": "6g", "mem_reservation": "4g"}}
    written to docker-compose.override.yml - for a stack running NEXT TO PRODUCTION on the same
    box, so a big rebuild cannot starve the live system. Change later with docker_stack_limits.

    `test_stack=true`: every conf gets max_cron_threads = 0 (a copy of production data must never
    run its scheduled jobs) and the 20+ services get ODOO_HTTP_SOCKET_TIMEOUT=10. Why: Odoo 20
    closes an idle HTTP socket after 2 seconds, which breaks screens over slow links (ssh
    tunnels, VPN). In production the answer is nginx with gzip + buffering in front
    (docker_domain does that); for direct access `http_socket_timeout` (seconds, 0 = Odoo's
    default) sets the variable on any stack.
name: docker_stack_init
